subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct according to the law of conservation of mass?

options.text: Mass can be created but cannot be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Mass can be created in a chemical reaction.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass can neither be created nor be destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The law of conservation of mass states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• This principle was established by Antoine Lavoisier in the 18th century.
 
• In a closed system, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
 
• The law applies to both physical changes and chemical reactions.
 
• This law is fundamental to the field of chemistry and underpins stoichiometric calculations in chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Definite Proportions**

 
 
• This law states that a chemical compound always contains the same proportion of elements by mass.
 
• It is also known as Proust's law.
 
 
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions**
 
 
• This law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in ratios of small whole numbers.
 
• It was formulated by John Dalton.
 
 
 
• **Stoichiometry**
 
 
• It involves the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is based on the laws of conservation of mass and definite proportions.
